transcript:
>> This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News in Washington, D.C.,
I'm Dale Willman.
President Trump rallied in the battleground state
of Georgia Saturday night.
It was his second visit to the state in eight days.
Robobali with member station WABE reports.
>> Despite recent polls and early voting trends,
including here in Georgia, Trump made this prediction.
>> We're going to crush the radical left Democrats
all across the country.
We're going to win the Republican House,
and we're going to win the Republican Senate
in record numbers.
People are going to be very surprised.
>> Trump took aim at two high-profile Democratic figures,
Georgia U.S. Senator John Ossoff
and Michigan Democratic nominee
for U.S. Senate Abdul Al Syed.
Both are from states won by Trump in 2024.
Former President Barack Obama
and former Vice President Kamala Harris
are set to make appearances in Georgia this week.
For NPR News, I'm Ronald Bali in Perry, Georgia.
>> Former President Barack Obama rallied Democratic voters
in the Midwest Saturday.
In Ohio, he talked about what he called the cruelty
and indecency coming from President Trump
and his Republican allies,
including an ad by Ohio gubernatorial candidate
Vivek Ramaswamy.
He has a controversial ad with the estranged mother
of his Democratic challenger, Dr. Amy Acton.
Obama said there is no low Ramaswamy will not sink to.
Obama also held a rally in Michigan.
The U.S. is easing tariffs on Canadian products
just ahead of the midterm elections,
and B.R.'s Chandelis Duster as more.
>> The Trump administration on Friday
said it will lift 50% tariffs on some Canadian products,
such as packing supplies, refrigerator equipment,
plywood sheets, and some paper products
will also have tariffs removed.
But other Canadian goods, such as waste products and carpets,
will have tariffs added.
By removing the tariffs, the White House says
President Trump is, quote,
"offsetting the burden to U.S. commerce
while better serving the public interest."
The U.S. and Canada have not reached an agreement on trade.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney told reporters on Friday
that the chance of a deal being reached
before the midterm elections is, quote, "up to the United States."
The new tariff changes will go into effect Friday, October 30th,
less than a week before the midterm elections.
Chandelis Duster, NPR News.
>> Hundreds of people have been rescued
from flooded homes along the San Juan River
near Farmington, New Mexico.
The efforts followed severe storms and flash flooding
across the southwestern U.S. that began Wednesday.
San Juan County Fire Chief David Vega
says crews continue to go door to door
to make sure no one else is trapped.
>> As the water's starting to recede in some areas,
that's gonna provide us an opportunity
for us to get crews in,
do a very slow, methodical surge of all the houses
to make sure that we haven't missed anything.
>> Weather officials say still more water surges
may happen this weekend.
You're listening to NPR News.
Six Flags says it will add secondary restraints
on its rides across the chain
that are similar to the roller coaster Goliath
at its Georgia Park.
That's where a man died after he was thrown from his seat,
Melissa Fato from member station WABE reports.
>> The seat belts similar to those worn in an airplane
or car will be used in addition
to the coaster's mechanical restraints, the company says.
Some Six Flags rides already use these type of restraints.
CEO John Riley did not specify
which attractions will get seat belts,
but eight other rides of the hyper coaster
and Giga coaster models manufactured by the Swiss firm
Bolliger and Mabelard remain closed across the chain.
Goliath also remains closed, depending, quote,
necessary safety reviews and clearances.
Officials are still investigating
what caused 42-year-old Hassan Karim's death
at Six Flags over Georgia.
This is the first major change the company has announced
since the accident earlier this month.
For NPR News, I'm Melissa Fato in Atlanta.
>> The Archdiocese of New York has agreed
to an $800 million settlement for about 1,300 parishioners
who say they were sexually abused by clergy.
The deal follows a 2024 settlement for Los Angeles.
One survivor says the agreement represents a powerful moment
in the pursuit of justice.
Saturday brought more upsets
to college football's top 10 teams.
Keyon Jones threw a two-yard touchdown pass
and the second overtime is unranked.
UCF beat number two BYU 39 to 31.
In Cincinnati, JC French the fourth
threw a career-high four touchdown passes
as the Bearcats stunned number eight Texas Tech 37 to 24.
And Georgia Fox beat Puget Sound 35 to 17.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.
>> This message comes from US Bank.
Chief Product Officer Shruti Patel shares
how US Bank business essentials combines business checking
and payments in one simple solution.
>> We wanted to make banking really easy for small business
and all of the time and cost we can save them
in their back office operations helps them focus more
on running their business more effectively
and serving the customer as well.
>> Learn more at usbank.com/business, member FDIC.

topics.text: Trump rallies in Georgia, predicts Republican wins and attacks Ossoff and Al Syed
Obama rallies Democratic voters in Ohio and Michigan, criticizes Trump and Vivek Ramaswamy's ad
Trump administration lifts some tariffs on Canadian products, adds others, ahead of midterms
Hundreds rescued from flooded homes along San Juan River near Farmington, New Mexico
Six Flags to add secondary seat belt restraints on rides after fatal Goliath accident in Georgia
Archdiocese of New York agrees to $800 million settlement with about 1,300 clergy abuse survivors
UCF upsets BYU in double overtime; Cincinnati stuns Texas Tech in college football upsets
